episodes.title: The heading
episodes.english: Year 1 of the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes, the seventh of the name⟩, {living, enduring, strong}. Went to the West the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes, the sixth of the name⟩, [Lord of the River and of the Two Banks], beloved of Uqa'a, {fire of Uqa'a upon the mound, who stood, who was crowned, lord of the count, whose seal is on the granary, whose grain the barges carry}, [given life like the sun forever], in his twenty-seventh year. His account is read.

episodes.title: Birth and crowning
episodes.english: Shaped him Uzn'era [in the womb], a child of the house of Zu'Meku. Stood he upon the mound [at Yath-Telgu]; {set the priesthood of Uqa'a the crown on him, and gave him his name, ⟨Meqes⟩; by this name every contract of the year is dated.} Qe'aret set truth in his mouth, and Reth'Sa'ar wrote his name [in the house of books]. The gods gave him life and dominion, like the sun.

episodes.title: The war of the west
episodes.english: Came down His Majesty, {the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes⟩, beloved of Uqa'a, Lord of the River and of the Two Banks, given life like the sun forever,} upon the hill-men of the western margins, and Chaq'ur raged before him like the storm. Smote he their chieftains, [took he their herds,] and brought back their princes bound [beneath his sandals]. {The margins were the Gar-Au's.}

episodes.title: The war of the north and the tribute
episodes.english: Sailed he, {the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes⟩, beloved of Uqa'a, given life like the sun forever,} against the raiders of the northern sea, and the fire of Uqa'a went out against their ships. The river was at peace, and the barges came up laden: gold, cedar, horses [and slaves]. {The river was the Gar-Au's.}

episodes.title: The great hunt and the lean years
episodes.english: Rode he out, {the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes⟩, beloved of Uqa'a, Lord of the River and of the Two Banks,} against the lions and the river-horses that ravaged the herds and the fields, and the beasts taken were counted. In the years of the low river he opened the god's granaries under his seal, which he had filled in the years of the flood, and none of his people hungered.

episodes.title: His works, the god's answer, and the weighing
episodes.english: {The Gar-Au ⟨Meqes⟩, beloved of Uqa'a,} built anew the house of Uqa'a, gave it altars of gold, and endowed it with fields and herds. [He raised his Way at the head of the death-road at Zu-Gezer.] [Words spoken by Uqa'a, {fire on the first ground, lord of the dry ink, who comes up the road}: “My beloved son, I give you every land, every foreign country bowed beneath your sandals; I give you the years of the sun upon the throne of the mound.”] Before the gods the tablets lay level on the beam: what he owed was closed, and nothing remained; what was owed to him stood open. He went down owed.

strong.title: living, enduring, strong
strong.note: From the stela's closing epithet. _Strong_ is 01-014, the standing man braced on a stave, whose consonants k-z are _kuz_, strong (the throne-name element in the Khelathi note).

countlord.title: lord of the count
countlord.note: The stela's _lord of the count_ is written _lord, of, the tally rod_ (01-013, 10-016, 13-035).

gravingseal.title: whose seal is on the granary, whose grain the barges carry
gravingseal.note: Written _his seal, upon, granary; grain, barge_ (15-010, 10-016, 11-004; 14-016, 12-014). The signet ring is the seal a man carries as his own. The relative _whose_ is unwritten.

account.title: his account
account.note: 04-018, the heart bound with a cord and sealed (h-l-z), is _halzi_: the heart and the account it answers for.

crown.title: set the crown on him
crown.note: The crown (15-007) alone writes the setting of it. The hand over the stand (04-011 : 03-025) writes _set_ only where Qe'aret sets truth; written here too, it would cost the line a quadrat.

contract.title: every contract
contract.note: 14-019, the sealed roll tied with a cord, is the base of the entry family and writes the contract, with the plural strokes. The stela names contracts, tax rolls and leases; only the contract is written. 14-031, the entry opened, would write _every entry made_ instead.

dated.title: is dated
dated.note: No sign means _to date_. The regnal-year sign (16-024) after _contract_ writes _of the year_, and the dating is read from it.

truth.title: truth
truth.note: No sign means truth. 13-033, the balance with two pans, is the level account that Qe'aret's own sign (03-006) also draws. It reads as _order_ at least as readily as _truth_.

dominion.title: dominion
dominion.note: 03-029, a hand of power within a ring, carries no stated word. Read as power held, it stands for dominion.

mine.title: was the Gar-Au's
mine.note: The stela's refrain _and the canal was his_ is written with the enthroned Gar-Au (01-060) after the thing taken: _the margins, the Gar-Au_.

cedar.title: cedar
cedar.note: No sign for cedar. 13-037, the log (l-g-n, _lagun_), means timber of any kind.

rode.title: rode out
rode.note: No chariot or rider is drawn. The horse (05-005) stands for riding out.

lions.title: the lions and the river-horses
lions.note: Written _lions, river-horses_, each with the plural strokes, in one quadrat. No sign writes _and_; the beasts are listed as the tribute's gold, cedar and horses are.

ravaged.title: that ravaged the herds and the fields
ravaged.note: No sign for ravaging. The line reads _the beasts of the herds and the fields_, and the scene carries the hunt.

count.title: the beasts taken were counted
count.note: Written with the tally rod (13-035). No number is given in the approved text, so none is written. A count in strokes and tens (16-003) can follow the tally if the owner names one.

opened.title: opened the granaries
opened.note: No sign for opening a store. The plain hand (04-011) stands for the act; the entry family's _open_ (14-034) names the state of an entry and does not write it.

filled.title: filled its storehouses
filled.note: Written with 14-016, the heap of grain, before the granary. No sign means _fill_.

people.title: his people
people.note: No sign for a people. 01-068, the standing man with empty hands (z-l-r, _zelar_, the commoner), with the plural strokes, writes the common folk.

hunger.title: none of his people hungered
hunger.note: No sign for hunger or its absence. Written _his people: bread and life_, with the loaf (14-007) and the sprout of life (08-005).

lapis.title: lapis
lapis.note: No sign for lapis or any blue stone, and none is coined. The register reads _altars of gold_; the render can paint the altar sign lapis blue to carry the rest.

endowed.title: endowed it
endowed.note: Written with 13-032, the stamp seal (q-th-r, _qathur_, the seal and the warrant it closes): fields and herds given by sealed warrant.

head.title: at the head of the death-road
head.note: No sign for the head of a road. Written _at the road of the dead_: 10-020 (path between two stones) with 10-014, the west, which also writes the dead, as determinative.

firstground.title: fire on the first ground
firstground.note: The hymn's _first ground_ is the primeval mound; 10-011 (mound on a flat) writes it.

comesup.title: who comes up the road
comesup.note: The hymn is sung on the eastern face before the sun is up the road, and _who comes up the road_ is the sun rising. 09-003, the disk rising between two hills, writes the coming up as the sunrise, and 10-020 the road.

son.title: my son
son.note: No sign means son. 01-067, a tall standing figure beside a small one (th-z), shows a parent with a child. The seated child (01-011) is the alternative.

every.title: every land, every foreign country
every.note: No sign for _every_. Written as plurals: lands, foreign countries.

level.title: the tablets level on the beam
level.note: 03-006 draws the Reading's _tablets level on the beam_ exactly, and it is also Qe'aret's sign. On a wall of the weighing both readings stand: the level account, and the goddess of the scale who holds it.
